requests.text: [formal, out of breath] Wait! Wolves in that den. Give me a moment. I ran all the way from the bend.
[straightening] I'm a squire with the Order of the Dawning Flame. They sent me to clear this road. No, there's no one else coming.
[reddening, honest] Nothing! This is my first errand. They said the road was quiet. I counted the tracks outside that den twice. Please don't tell the Order I asked for help.
[honest] I've only fought in the training yard. Straw doesn't come at you in a pack. Could you stay?

[earnest] Knights sworn to the sun. Our chapter house is down in the sun-lands, where I grew up. I still turn east when I pray, even under all these trees. They sent me north to learn the roads. I hadn't expected to be grateful for strangers this soon.
[reddening, then honest] Sword practice. Prayers. They didn't put teeth on the practice dummy. With respect, are you going to help?
[relieved] God keep you. Give me a moment to tighten this strap. All right. Stay behind my shield.
[formal, hurt] I see. God go with you. I'll wait until they come out. One at a time, I hope.
[uneasy] Burning Gauntlet. What's a city patrol doing down here? They've got a woman at sword-point. I don't recognise her dress.
[formal, tight] Which goddess, señora? Tell me her name before I draw my weapon.
[quietly] Yes, it matters to me. are we stepping in? I'll follow your lead here.
[quietly] I've prayed over this every night. I still can't accept the company we're keeping. If I stay, we'll have this same argument at every fire. I'm leaving.
[formal] I'll be at the Open Hand. If you part ways with them, come and find me. I'd like to ride with you again. God keep you.
[low] Let her wait. You don't owe her an answer just because she's frightened.
[hesitant] In the yard, you could put your hand up and stop the bout. I miss that.
[honest] I pray before we fight. Then I look for somewhere to run. Haven't done it yet. I'm afraid I will.
[relieved] Thank you. You've stood beside me. I'll try to remember that when I start worrying again.
[easier] I wrote to Mother. Told her about you. Left out the fighting, or she'd walk all the way here to fetch me.
[fond] She has a bakery. I used to carry flour before dawn and complain about the weight. I'd give a good deal to be back there tomorrow morning.
[warm] She's kept my stool by the oven. I used to sleep there between deliveries. Apparently my bedroom was too far away when she needed another sack.
[shy] Yes. I'd like that. Could we take our time? There's still so much I don't know about you.
[gentle] All right. I won't keep asking. Come and sit with me later, if you'd like.
[nervous] I've been looking forward to our evenings together. Even when I'm too tired to say much.
[earnest] Would you have supper with me when we get a night to ourselves? I'd like to take you somewhere decent.
[pleased] Good. I know a place. And if I salute you at the table, please pretend you didn't see it.
[bravely] All right. I'm glad you told me plainly. I won't bring it up again.
[shouting] Dawning Flame, keep my hand steady!
[earnest] Get behind my shield! Now!
[strained] Caught the mail. I'm standing. Keep going!
